classification.difficultyReason: Requires an exhaustive classification of reciprocal shapes using the possible positions of an unspecified parabola.

inlines.text: Let
be a concave up parabola. Sketch all possible shapes of
Vertex above the x-axis: one positive hump, with no vertical asymptotes.
Vertex below the x-axis: two positive outer branches and one negative central branch, with two vertical asymptotes.
Vertex on the x-axis: two positive branches, with one vertical asymptote.
Use the parabola’s zeroes and signs. All three shapes have horizontal asymptote
. Sketches are shown in the same order.
Write
, where
and the vertex is
. Classify the graph by the vertex’s position relative to the x-axis.
: the parabola is always positive and has no zeroes. Its reciprocal is a positive hump with maximum
and no vertical asymptotes.
: the two zeroes become vertical asymptotes at
. The reciprocal is positive outside them and negative between them. The central branch has maximum
and approaches negative infinity at both asymptotes.
: the single zero becomes a vertical asymptote at
. Both branches are positive and approach positive infinity there.
In every case, the parabola’s large positive y-values become small positive y-values, so the reciprocal approaches
from above at both ends. Join the features smoothly; the three sketches illustrate the cases in order.

spec.description: A positive hump with a maximum on its symmetry axis, tending towards the x-axis at both ends; black axes and a blue reciprocal curve, with no numerical ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Representative case f(x)=x^2+1, plotted as y=1/(x^2+1). The numerical parameters illustrate a valid shape and are not source givens.

spec.sourceRegion: Q46; teacher PDF2, enrichment Q46, second sketch
spec.description: Two dashed vertical asymptotes, positive outer branches and a negative central branch with a maximum. No numerical ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Representative case f(x)=x^2-1, plotted as y=1/(x^2-1). The illustrative asymptotes are x=-1 and x=1; these values are not source givens.

spec.sourceRegion: Q46; teacher PDF2, enrichment Q46, third sketch
spec.description: Two positive branches tending upwards beside the y-axis and towards the x-axis at the outer ends. The y-axis coincides with the vertical asymptote. No numerical ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Representative case f(x)=x^2, plotted as y=1/x^2 for x not equal to zero. The vertex location is illustrative, not a source given.
